what: Supreme Court of India, In Re: Inhuman Conditions in 1382 Prisons, W.P.(C) No. 406/2013, record of proceedings and order of 23 August 2024 (Hima Kohli and Sandeep Mehta JJ.). The order the owner's file gives as the key authority of Q6 (BNSS s.479).
text_tool: pdftotext (poppler), default mode, pages separated by form feeds, no edits

verified_by_reading.case_and_date: W.P.(C) 406/2013, IN RE-INHUMAN CONDITIONS IN 1382 PRISONS, dated 23-08-2024; CORAM Hon'ble Ms. Justice Hima Kohli and Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sandeep Mehta: matches the owner's file
verified_by_reading.content: Paras 1-7: the amicus pointed to the first proviso to s.479 BNSS (first-time offender released on bond after one-third of the maximum term); the ASG, on the Department's instructions, said the provision applies to all undertrials in pending cases irrespective of whether the case was registered before 1 July 2024; the Court directs immediate implementation: jail superintendents to process applications on completion of one-half/one-third; steps within two months; affidavits from States/UTs; District and Sessions Judges in charge of the Under Trial Review Committees to see to compliance; listed 22 Oct 2024.
verified_by_reading.difference_from_the_owners_expected_answ: The owner's file says the Supreme Court 'held' that s.479 applies to undertrials whose cases were registered before 1 July 2024. The order records the Union's stated position (instructions from the Department) and directs implementation; it does not give reasons or say 'held'. The exclusion of offences punishable with death or life imprisonment is the statute's (s.479(1)), not stated in this order. [Certain, from the text]
